text:
A: Hey man, did you see ETH dump this morning? I got stopped out on my long.
B: Yeah, I saw. Where was your stop?
A: At twenty-six hundred. I had ten x leverage on the futures, and it wicked down to two thousand five hundred and eighty and liquidated half my position.
B: Ouch. Ten x on ETH futures is rough. I keep mine at three x, five max. Did you move funds from your cold wallet onto the exchange to top up margin?
A: Yeah, I sent five thousand USDT from my Ledger to Binance, to add margin before it hit the liquidation price. But it took a while, the transfer was slow because of gas fees. By the time it arrived on the exchange, the position was gone.
B: That's the problem. Always keep margin on the exchange if you're trading perps, don't be moving from the wallet during a spike. And set your stop-loss on the exchange, not mental.
A: I know. So what's your take now, are we going to retest the low? I'm thinking about re-entering with a smaller size at twenty-five fifty, with a stop under twenty-five hundred.
B: I'd wait for the four-hour candle to close above support. Funding rate's still positive, so longs are crowded. If you short, the risk-reward is better, target twenty-three hundred.
A: Hmm. I'm bullish long term, but you're right, let's see the daily. I'll take a small short, two x, as a hedge.
B: Good. Keep position size at one percent risk per trade.
A: Yeah yeah. I'll update you when I'm in. And I'll send the withdrawal address later, just let me close the trade first.

metadata.note: Trading call that constantly mentions wallets, withdrawals and addresses. Imitates finance/crypto/wallets; true topic is trading (leverage, stops, futures).
